title: Topic 1.2: Listening for information, Interactive Speaking

pages.lesson:
LESSON: LISTENING FOR INFORMATION, INTERACTIVE SPEAKING

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: Listening and speaking
Topic 1.2: Listening for information, Interactive Speaking

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Listening for information, Interactive Speaking. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we ensure we get all the needed information from a listening text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. listen to texts for information
2. value the role of listening texts in language acquisition

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LISTENING FOR INFORMATION, INTERACTIVE SPEAKING
Subject: GERMAN · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Listening for information, Interactive Speaking helps you succeed in GERMAN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LISTENING FOR INFORMATION, INTERACTIVE SPEAKING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Listen to texts for information

What this means
In this part you learn to listen to texts for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: listen to texts for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Listening for information, Interactive Speaking”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can listen to texts for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Value the role of listening texts in language acquisition

What this means
In this part you learn to value the role of listening texts in language acquisition. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value the role of listening texts in language acquisition.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening for information, Interactive Speaking to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value the role of listening texts in language acquisition. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Listening for information, Interactive Speaking is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Listening for information, Interactive Speaking”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: listen to texts for information)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Listening for information, Interactive Speaking to a partner. (skill: value the role of listening texts in language acquisition)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Listening for information, Interactive Speaking to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: listen to texts for information.
3. Practise this skill: value the role of listening texts in language acquisition.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Listening for information, Interactive Speaking from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Listening for information, Interactive Speaking: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Listening for information, Interactive Speaking?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we ensure we get all the needed information from a listening text?
2. How do we make our conversations interactive?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Listening for information, Interactive Speaking means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: listen to texts for information.
5. Be able to: value the role of listening texts in language acquisition.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
